Digital artist nohygiene creates surreal 3D characters that combine angelic imagery, early-internet aesthetics and intensely emotional scenes. Her recurring figures have oversized heads, metallic or pale bodies, long hair and wings. They appear alone, exhausted, in love or overwhelmed, while simple symbols such (Artvangarde)as hearts, fire and tears make their emotions immediately visible. The deliberately imperfect graphics recall early 3D animation, online avatars and old computer imagery, rather than the polished realism of contemporary CGI. Across her work, these strange digital beings (Artvangarde)become vessels for very human feelings love, loneliness, anxiety, desire and emotional vulnerability. #art #loveyou #artist #niche #heart

Digitals that got me REJECTED vs. Digitals that got me SIGNED. 📸 Two years ago, I was getting rejected by modeling agencies. Today, I’m professionally signed in Paris and Milan. Here’s what I’ve learned along the way and what I wish I knew before submitting my first digitals: 1. SHOW YOUR NATURAL HAIR This was one of my biggest mistakes. Avoid overly styled hair, excessive products, or getting a fresh skin fade just for your digitals. Agencies want to see your natural hair, hairline, and overall potential. Keep it clean, natural, and simple. 2. TAKE CARE OF YOUR SKIN Your skin matters more than you think. Agencies want to see your natural complexion, skin texture, and facial features. Build a consistent skincare routine and take care of active breakouts. You don’t need perfect skin, but good grooming and healthy-looking skin can make a difference. 3. SHOW SOME PERSONALITY Don’t look like a robot. A lot of beginners look extremely stiff and uncomfortable in their digitals. Relax your shoulders, maintain good posture, and show some confidence. Stay professional, but don’t be afraid to show a natural expression. 4. KEEP YOUR FACE CLEAN-SHAVEN For male models, I recommend starting with a clean-shaven look unless the agency specifically requests otherwise. Facial hair can hide your jawline and facial structure. The goal is to make your natural features as visible as possible. 5. WEAR SIMPLE, FITTED CLOTHING Forget designer outfits, oversized shirts, and flashy accessories. A fitted black or white T-shirt with simple jeans is usually enough. I personally prefer black because it creates a clean contrast with my features. Your clothes should highlight your proportions, not distract from them. 6. LIGHTING AND ANGLES MATTER You don’t need an expensive camera or professional studio. Natural daylight, a plain background, and a good phone camera are enough. Take clear front-facing, side-profile, and full-body shots. Avoid dramatic angles, harsh shadows, and distorted perspectives. 7. NO FILTERS, NO RETOUCHING This is extremely important. Agencies want to see the REAL you. No skin smoothing, face reshaping, beauty filters, or heavy editing. Digitals are supposed to show your natural potential, not an edited version of yourself. Remember: Getting rejected doesn’t necessarily mean you don’t have modeling potential. Sometimes your presentation needs improvement, and sometimes you simply aren’t the right fit for that agency. These are the things that helped me improve my digitals and eventually get signed. Keep improving, stay consistent, and don’t let rejection stop you. Save this before submitting your next digitals. #model #modeling #digitals #selfimprovement

¿Qué es el arte digital? 🌐      Cuando hablamos de arte digital la tecnología no tiene que ser el único medio de creación, con el simple hecho de que haya una intervención tecnológica, o algún elemento añadido con el ordenador, la pieza es considerada digital. Esta forma de arte puede ser generada totalmente por una computadora, escaneada, dibujada o editada utilizando un mouse o una tableta.        El arte es, pues, ante todo, experiencia. Sensaciones como resultado de pensamientos compartidos, que juntos conforman experiencias. Ciencia, tecnología y arte confluyen en la experiencia artística.      ¿Qué te parece este concepto?       #arte #artecontemporáneo #artedigital #comunicacióndigital #digitalización #museodigital #arteentiktok #pintura #videoedit #cccreator #viral #fyp #tutorial #vlog #aprendeentiktok #tiktokdesign #tiktokart #artistiktok #artisttiktok #tiktokartist

This digital camera basically feels like a compact camera crossed with a Game Boy, and that’s exactly why it caught my attention. Dinooh has no playback, a mechanical advance lever, four built-in film filters, and a tiny screen that plays animations instead of showing you the photo.
